text.p: Italian bonds and BTP futures slipped back to hold in negative territory in late afternoon trading reflecting profit taking after recent strong gains and the lower tone to other bond markets, dealers said.

Futures had been driven higher early by the strong lira and the higher dollar and optimism that Italy will be in Europe's single currency from the start, and the September LIFFE contract hit a fresh high of 137.10 in early trading.
"After a strong start, caution crept in as the market was seen to be going up too fast too soon, while the lower tone to bunds weighed on sentiment," said one LIFFE dealer.

Dealers said that the warning by the EU Commissioner Mario Monti of the dangers of being swept away by the euphoria of rising expectations that Italy will join the currency union may have helped halt the BTP rally.

Monti said that Italy had made big progress since the end of 1996 in improving its finances but one should not be blinded by euphoria. He said in a newspaper interview that it was not a foregone conclusion that Italy would be let into EMU.
The continued strength in the lira prompted intervention by the Bank of Italy according to foreign exchange dealers.

One dealer said the Italian central bank had bought German marks at 970.70 lire and then at 970.80 lire, and dealers added that they believed the central bank wanted the Italian currency to stabilise around the 970-971 lire/mark area.
Earlier, the lira had touched a high of 969.95 lire/mark helped by the rally in the dollar. The lira was last quoted at 970.70/971.10 lire/mark by 1545 GMT from 973.89 lire Friday.
